clue.text: One maybe taking Jersey leader around street

definitions.note: a Jersey is a breed of cow, so a cattle thief is one who might take it

indicators.note: the word for a leader is placed around the street abbreviation, enclosing it

parts.note: a ruler is a leader

explanation.surface: Someone, perhaps a politician, takes the leader of Jersey for a walk around a street.
explanation.walkthrough: Jersey looks like the Channel Island or a sweater; here it is a breed of dairy cow, and 'maybe' marks it as an example of what is stolen.
explanation.definitionFit: A rustler is a cattle thief, and a Jersey cow is one example of livestock such a thief might steal.

clue.text: Cheat runs away after international pressure

indicators.note: the word for away is placed after the letters for international and pressure

parts.note: R is the cricket scoring abbreviation for runs
P is the physics abbreviation for pressure
off means away, as in 'he's off'

explanation.surface: A swindler escapes abroad under pressure from international authorities.
explanation.definitionFit: A rip-off is a swindle or fraud, so it is a noun synonym for a cheat.

clue.text: Still showing sign of nerves supporting short celebrity

indicators.note: in a down clue, supporting means placed underneath the other part
short means the word for a celebrity loses its last letter

parts.note: a star is a celebrity
a tic is a nervous twitch

explanation.surface: A small celebrity still shows nervous twitches while backing someone up.
explanation.definitionFit: Static describes something not moving, a synonym for still as an adjective.

clue.text: Fruit if gone off could make Beryl groan

indicators.note: if the fruit's letters went off, as rotten fruit does, they would rearrange into the two named words

parts.note: the ten letters that the fruit's name rearranges into

explanation.surface: Rotten fruit would make a woman called Beryl groan in disgust.
explanation.walkthrough: This is read in reverse: the answer, if its letters 'go off' (are scrambled), could make BERYL GROAN.
explanation.definitionFit: The loganberry is a hybrid berry, a cross between a raspberry and a blackberry, so a kind of fruit.

clue.text: Artist put on Ken Loach film for playboys

indicators.note: in a down clue, the artist goes on top of the film title

parts.note: RA is a Royal Academician, a crossword artist
Kes is a 1969 film directed by Ken Loach about a boy and his kestrel

explanation.surface: A painter stages a showing of a Ken Loach film for some wealthy playboys.
explanation.definitionFit: A rake is a dissolute man about town, so rakes are pleasure-seeking playboys.

clue.text: Lass changed trousers and shoes

indicators.note: used as a verb: the rearranged letters pocket the word and, as trousers would
changed means the letters of lass are rearranged

parts.note: the four letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A girl swapped her trousers for some new shoes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Trousers' reads as clothing but is a verb here meaning pockets, as a pair of trousers holds things.
explanation.definitionFit: Sandals are open shoes held on with straps, a type of footwear.

clue.text: Fancy trifle

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a notion or hunch, as in 'I have a fancy he's lying'

explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests the British dessert; trifle here is a small trace.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both a vague belief or hunch and a slight trace or hint of something.

clue.text: Trouble after fourth of brandies — one might get hammered

indicators.note: the word for trouble comes after the picked letter
fourth of means take the fourth letter of the word brandies

parts.note: to ail is to trouble, as an illness does

explanation.surface: After a few brandies, someone in trouble might get hammered, meaning very drunk.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hammered' suggests drunkenness, fitting the brandies, but it means struck by a hammer.
explanation.definitionFit: A nail is driven in by a hammer, so it is a thing that gets struck with one.

clue.text: Mixture of gar and tuna I cooked with breadcrumbs

indicators.note: a mixture blends the following words' letters together

parts.note: taken as written; a gar is a fish

explanation.surface: A recipe: a fish mix of garfish and tuna that I have cooked, topped with breadcrumbs.
explanation.definitionFit: Au gratin describes a dish topped with a browned crust of breadcrumbs or cheese.

clue.text: Police officer wants unwrapped fabric on the top

indicators.note: in a down clue the fabric sits on top of the other part

parts.note: serge is a hard-wearing woollen fabric

indicators.note: unwrapped means the outer letters of wants are removed

explanation.surface: A police officer wants some fabric uncovered on top of something.
explanation.definitionFit: A sergeant is a police rank above constable, so a type of police officer.

clue.text: Collision from parking next to Sierra? Almost

indicators.note: the parking letter is placed next to the shortened mountain chain

parts.note: P is the road-sign abbreviation for parking

indicators.note: almost means the last letter is dropped

parts.note: a sierra is a mountain range

explanation.surface: A minor crash happened while parking beside a Ford Sierra, or nearly did.
explanation.walkthrough: Sierra suggests the Ford car (fitting a car park) or the NATO letter S, but it is a mountain range. A prang is British slang for a minor car crash.
explanation.definitionFit: Prang is informal British slang for a minor accident in a car, a bump or crash.

clue.text: US diplomat gently touching her husband's cut

parts.note: kissing is touching gently with the lips

indicators.note: cut means a letter is removed from the word her

parts.note: H is the abbreviation for husband

explanation.surface: A woman gently touches her husband's cut, a domestic scene.
explanation.walkthrough: Henry Kissinger was US Secretary of State in the 1970s.
explanation.definitionFit: Henry Kissinger was the famous American Secretary of State and National Security Adviser.

clue.text: Camaraderie from devotees bandaging right hip

indicators.note: the word for devotees wraps around the letter for right, as a bandage would

parts.note: fiends are enthusiasts or devotees, as in 'fitness fiends'

explanation.surface: Fans show camaraderie by bandaging someone's injured right hip.
explanation.definitionFit: Friendship is the bond of fellowship between friends, a close synonym of camaraderie.

clue.text: China tea

definitions.meaning: first meaning: china plate is Cockney rhyming slang for ..., a friend
second meaning: a caffeinated South American herbal infusion made from yerba leaves

explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests China tea; in Cockney rhyming slang 'china plate' means a mate, so china is a friend.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is British slang for a friend and also the name of an infused herbal drink from South America.

clue.text: Leadership from chap, a shining example on hospital department

indicators.note: in a down clue the earlier pieces sit on top of the department

parts.note: a chap is a man
a gem is a prized or outstanding example
ENT is the ear, nose and throat department

explanation.surface: Leadership is shown by a man who is a shining example in a hospital department.
explanation.definitionFit: Management means the people in charge of running an organisation, its directing body.

clue.text: Organise Persia trip? No sweat

indicators.note: to organise is to arrange, so these letters are put into a new order

explanation.surface: Planning a trip to Persia is no sweat, meaning no trouble at all.
explanation.walkthrough: 'No sweat' reads as a phrase meaning easy; 'No' is in fact fodder and 'sweat' alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Perspiration is the fluid excreted through the skin, the formal word for sweat.

clue.text: Doctor is Mary ill in the same way?

indicators.note: used as a verb: to doctor is to tamper with, so the letters are reworked

explanation.surface: Asking a doctor whether Mary is ill in the same way as someone else.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Doctor' reads as a physician fitting 'ill', but it is a verb meaning tamper with.
explanation.definitionFit: Similarly is an adverb meaning likewise, or in a like manner.

clue.text: Grasping pound, getting paid

parts.note: L is the abbreviation for pound sterling, from Latin libra
earning is getting paid for work

explanation.surface: A greedy person grasping every pound they get paid.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Grasping' suggests greed; it means understanding, as in grasping a concept.
explanation.definitionFit: Learning is the act of coming to understand something, which is what grasping an idea means.

clue.text: Old maid cuts up their odd bits only

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the word is read from bottom to top

parts.note: snips are small cuts

indicators.note: only the odd-numbered letters of the word their are kept

explanation.surface: An old maid trims their clothes, cutting up only odd scraps.
explanation.definitionFit: Spinster is a dated term for an unmarried woman, the kind once called an old maid.

clue.text: Expert male in criminal trial

definitions.note: used attributively, as in 'a trial run', an adjective sense

indicators.note: criminal suggests something wrong or twisted, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: An expert man gives evidence in a criminal trial.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Criminal trial' reads as one phrase, but the court sense is a red herring: 'criminal' signals the anagram, and 'trial' means a test.
explanation.definitionFit: Something experimental is done as a test or on a trial basis, as in an experimental scheme.

clue.text: Words of sympathy due here, by the sound of it

indicators.note: by the sound of it says the phrase is heard rather than spelt

parts.note: due means owed, so the phrase is owed here

explanation.surface: A sympathetic word is apparently owed to someone here.
explanation.definitionFit: Oh dear is an exclamation expressing dismay or commiseration at someone's misfortune.

clue.text: Pictured an injury, getting cross, and raged after a change of heart

parts.note: X is a cross shape

indicators.note: the middle letter, the heart, of raged is swapped for another

explanation.surface: Someone got cross and raged at an injury, then changed their mind.
explanation.walkthrough: The heart of RAGED is its middle letter G; changing it to Y gives RAYED.
explanation.definitionFit: To X-ray a broken bone is to take a radiographic image of it, so it means photographed the damage.

clue.text: Utterly offensive order

definitions.meaning: second meaning: a level or grade in a hierarchy

explanation.walkthrough: The two parts read as one complaint; they are separate meanings of the same word.
explanation.definitionFit: The word works as an adjective for foul or flagrant and as a noun for a position or grade in a hierarchy.

clue.text: Low female voice — understand the woman completely

parts.note: alto is the lower female singing voice
to get something is to understand it
her refers to a woman

explanation.surface: A singer with a low voice says she understands the woman completely.
explanation.definitionFit: Altogether is an adverb meaning totally or entirely.

clue.text: Animal more fashionable in the East End?

indicators.note: Cockneys of London's East End are said to drop their aitches, so the word loses its H

parts.note: hotter means more trendy or in vogue

explanation.surface: An animal is more fashionable in East London.
explanation.walkthrough: The East End is the traditional Cockney area of London, whose speakers drop the H sound at the start of words.
explanation.definitionFit: The otter is a fish-eating aquatic mammal of rivers and coasts.

clue.text: Region in Far East

indicators.note: in means the answer sits inside the letters of the two words

explanation.surface: A region located somewhere in the Far East.
explanation.definitionFit: An area is a district or zone, a synonym for a region.

clue.text: Bury dog, perhaps, assuming relatives initially understand

parts.note: to inter is to bury a body

indicators.note: assuming means taking on, so the pet word takes in the letter

parts.note: a dog is an example of a pet

indicators.note: initially means the first letter of relatives

explanation.surface: Bury the family dog, with relatives' grasp of the situation assumed.
explanation.definitionFit: To interpret is to explain or make sense of something, which means to understand it.

clue.text: Some military men eventually repelled foe

indicators.note: repelled means driven back, so the letters are read backwards
some means only part of the following words is taken

explanation.surface: Soldiers eventually drove back the enemy forces.
explanation.definitionFit: An enemy is a hostile opponent, the same as a foe.

clue.text: Country for example returning first of refugees — then a great number

indicators.note: returning means the abbreviation is read backwards

parts.note: EG is the abbreviation for for example, from Latin exempli gratia

indicators.note: first of means only the opening letter of refugees

parts.note: many means a great number

explanation.surface: A country, for example, sees refugees returning, then a great number more.
explanation.definitionFit: Germany is a nation in central Europe.

clue.text: Royal Engineers, worn out, stopped work

parts.note: RE is the abbreviation for the Royal Engineers, a British Army corps
worn out means tired

explanation.surface: Army engineers, exhausted, finally downed tools.
explanation.definitionFit: Retired describes someone who has left employment for good, which means they have ceased working.
